text.p: These are the main stories in Latvian newspapers on Tuesday. Prepared for Reuters by the Co-operation Fund. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- The prosecutor's office is expected this week to publish its conclusions on whether MPs breached anti-corruption laws.

- Parliament speaker Alfreds Chepanis, deputy speaker Andris Ameriks, Finance Minister Robert Zile and MP Aristids Lemberg may have broken anti-corruption by receiving a salary for being members of state-owned company boards.

- Nils Muizhnieks, the director of the Centre for Human Rights and Ethnic Studies, points out that the new government declaration says almost nothing about the recommendations made by the European Commission to Latvia.
- President Guntis Ulmanis is to return from his visit to the U.S. for the first cabinet meeting.

- Transport Minister Vilis Krishtopans held his first news conference after being re-appointed as minister of communications. He said the ministry will focus on restructuring railways, the transit of Russian goods and air traffic issues.
- A court is to consider a suit by Russian Lukoil Baltija against Ventspils Nafta, claiming compensation of $100,000 for being denied the use of berths at the oil terminal.
